plugin.name: Caddy services
plugin.help: Caddy logins and public routes: users are stored as bcrypt hashes, services.json turns http.in webhooks, local proxies and root site services into generated snippets your Caddyfile imports. It never edits the Caddyfile and only reloads Caddy when you press the button.
plugin.usage:
**What it does**

- Stores the Caddy Basic-Auth users in `users.json` (bcrypt only) and writes `caddy-users.conf`.
- Stores public services in `services.json` and writes `caddy-services.conf` (webhooks/proxies) plus `caddy-sites.conf` (root sites on their own port).
- Runs `caddy validate` before `caddy reload`, and only when you press the button.

**Caddyfile (once)**

```
home.example.com {
    import /opt/iobroker/iobroker-data/files/ihome.meta/external-access/caddy-services.conf

    handle {
        basic_auth {
            import /opt/iobroker/iobroker-data/files/ihome.meta/external-access/caddy-users.conf
        }
        reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8082
    }
}
```

The services import must come **before** the catch-all `handle` (Caddy `handle`
blocks are first-match). The card writes `caddy-services.conf`; never edit the
Caddyfile from this plugin. The snippet uses `basic_auth` (Caddy 2.8+); on older
Caddy use `basicauth` in your own Caddyfile.

**Webhook service**

Exposes one `http.in` endpoint without Basic Auth, protected only by its token:
`https://…/phone-event?token=…`. The token stays in the `http.in` plugin settings;
rotate it in the card and copy the new link.

**Proxy service**

Exposes a local upstream behind the Basic-Auth users, e.g. `/opencode` →
`127.0.0.1:49374`. `strip prefix` turns `/opencode/*` into `/*` for the app.
Only loopback and private upstreams are accepted.

**Site service**

Exposes an upstream at its own root on a dedicated port, for apps that do not
support a subpath (e.g. OpenCode's web UI). Pick `Basic Auth` or `upstream auth`
(the app authenticates itself, e.g. OpenCode's pairing links). The card shows the
link `https://<host>:<port>/`. Import `caddy-sites.conf` once at the **top level**
of the Caddyfile (outside the site block) and forward the port in the router. The
site address uses the hostname from the public URL.

Never expose ioBroker Admin, the ioBroker socket or Caddy's own admin API as a
service.

Use `https://…` for external access. `tls internal` instead of a public domain
works for a LAN-only HTTPS setup (the browser warns about the local CA).

**Install Caddy**

- Linux: https://caddyserver.com/docs/install#debian-ubuntu-raspbian (apt repo), then `systemctl enable --now caddy`.
- Windows: `winget install CaddyServer.Caddy` or `choco install caddy`; run `caddy run --config C:/caddy/Caddyfile` as a service.
- macOS: `brew install caddy`; `brew services start caddy`.

**Verify**

```
caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
caddy reload  --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
curl -I https://home.example.com/ihome/
```

Router: forward TCP 443 (and 80 for the ACME challenge) to the host running Caddy.
The user list here is only the Basic-Auth list; it does not create ioBroker users.

tiles.name: OpenCode pairing
tiles.description: Generate a one-time OpenCode pairing link for a Caddy site.
tiles.help:
Generates a one-time OpenCode pairing link for one of the site services in Caddy services.

**Before applying:** install and enable the Caddy services plugin, and configure the OpenCode site (for example `site-8444`). The plugin must stay installed and enabled for this tile to answer.

The tile offers the external (HTTPS) link and, when OpenCode reports a LAN address, the local plain-HTTP link. Each link works once and expires after five minutes.

options.html:
OpenCode pairing

One-time link; expires in 5 minutes. Open it on the other device. LAN is plain HTTP.
